articles.title: Five Storage Rules for GPT Summarization Workflow — Combining Batch Processing in Game Reviews
articles.excerpt: Short answer: store the review unit, its source digest, the prompt/schema version, the submission manifest, and the terminal result as separate records. A batch is useful only when a worker can restar…
articles.body: Short answer: store the review unit, its source digest, the prompt/schema version, the submission manifest, and the terminal result as separate records. A batch is useful only when a worker can restart without guessing which game-code changes were already summarized. The model API is one stage in that process; it is not the system of record. For a gaming team reviewing changes to gameplay code, the practical output is a structured finding, not a paragraph that happens to look sensible. I would use a batched workflow when reviews may wait, then make publication conditional on three checks: the result belongs to the intended change, it matches the declared schema, and every input has a terminal state. That choice favors recoverability over the pleasant simplicity of one request per diff.

articles.title: Git Hooks Not Running for Teammates? Husky vs Lefthook vs pre-commit
articles.excerpt: Git hooks don't run for teammates because .git/hooks/ is never committed, so every clone starts with no hooks at all. Husky, lefthook, and pre-commit all solve this the same way: the hook definitions…
articles.body: Git hooks don't run for teammates because .git/hooks/ is never committed, so every clone starts with no hooks at all. Husky, lefthook, and pre-commit all solve this the same way: the hook definitions live in the repo, and an install step points Git at them. Pick husky if your repo is already a Node project, lefthook if you want one fast binary with no runtime dependency, and pre-commit if your team is Python-heavy or wants a large catalog of ready-made hooks. Why do hooks work on my machine but not on a teammate's? The symptom is boring and easy to miss: a teammate pushes code that your pre-commit lint would have rejected, and nobody sees an error, because nothing ran. There is no failure to find.

articles.excerpt: You can ask Claude, Codex or Cursor what is slowing your Mac down, and get an answer from live data instead of generic advice. You need an MCP server on your Mac that reports what is running. Register…
articles.body: You can ask Claude, Codex or Cursor what is slowing your Mac down, and get an answer from live data instead of generic advice. You need an MCP server on your Mac that reports what is running. Register it once, and the assistant can call it whenever you ask. I built one into Binnacle, my menu bar monitor, called binnacle-mcp . Here is how the setup works and what it can and can't do. Why can't an assistant just answer this itself? Because it can't see your machine. Ask "why is my fan loud?" in a plain chat and you get a list of guesses: close tabs, check Activity Monitor, reset the SMC. Nothing in that answer comes from your Mac. An assistant that can run top in a terminal gets closer, but top lists processes.

articles.title: Repo Requiem: I Built an Obituary Writer for Abandoned Repositories
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine. Last October I published a small Puppeteer plugin called cloudflare-clearance-plugin. It took three da…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine . What I Built Last October I published a small Puppeteer plugin called cloudflare-clearance-plugin . It took three days, eight commits, and one README. Then I stopped. A year later the repository is still there: three branches, zero tags, 362 days of silence. I used to think of it as dead code. This week I realized it is not dead — it is quiet, and I am the only one who remembers what it was for. Repo Requiem is a command-line tool that gives a repository like that a funeral. Point it at a local git clone and it reads the history, then asks Gemma through Ollama to write an obituary: an epitaph, a short eulogy, a cause of death, last words, and what the project left behind.

articles.body: On Episode 234 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Mike Wall are joined by Than Putzig of the Planetary Science Institute about a NASA-backed payload bound for the Marius Hills Pit on the moon. In our ongoing quest to develop a moon base, could we possibly utilize the area beneath the surface of the moon in order to make the moon habitable? Could Marius Hills Pit, a roughly 50-meter-wide opening that may lead into a lunar lava tube, become the Moon's first living habitat for humans? Putzig explains how geophysical instruments on a rover could detect hidden voids beneath the surface and measure the size of these lava tubes.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

From Saturn's spectacular rings to shooting stars and even a space station flyover, the night sky has a few treats of its own in store for U.S. skywatchers on Oct. 31. Based on the latest national forecast, skies will be mainly clear on Saturday evening over most of New York State, northeast Pennsylvania, northern New Jersey and New England as well as a swath of the southern and central Great Plains, central Rockies, a portion of the Pacific Northwest and central and south Florida, as costumed kids arrive at the door looking for candy or some other Halloween treat.
articles.author: Joe Rao

articles.title: Happy Halloween! SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites to orbit from California (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX sent another batch of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit from California just after midnight on Halloween (Oct. 31).
articles.body: SpaceX celebrated Halloween with an early-morning launch from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today (Oct. 31) at 12:04 a.m. EDT (0404 GMT; 9:04 p.m. on Oct. 30 local time), sending 27 of the company's Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO). The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth as planned, touching down about 8.5 minutes after launch on the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base just after midnight ET on Oct. 31, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) It was the 18th flight for this particular booster, which is designated B1093.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
articles.author: Dan Goodin
